messages:
bob_merchant: Hey team — after rotating our API key this morning, our 10% of requests to Redwood are now failing with 401 invalid_api_key. We rotated keys via the dashboard at 08:12 UTC. Some hosts show success, others 401. Can you help?

alice_support: Sorry for the trouble, bob — looking. Do you have a sample failing request (curl or SDK) and a response body? Also did you rotate the key for the same org/project or create a new key under another service account?

bob_merchant: We replaced the key in our k8s secret and restarted the app pods. Here's a failing curl from one of the hosts:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_oldkey_that_was_rotated" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"gpt-x","input":"hi"}'
```

Response
```
HTTP/2 401
{"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key"}}
```

alice_support: OK thanks. Two quick checks: 1) can you confirm the pod showing 401 definitely loaded the new secret (kubectl exec + echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY)? 2) Any proxies/load-balancers in front of your pods?

bob_merchant: Confirmed new secret value in container env on the failing host. No customer-side proxy besides our cloud LB. We do have an internal sidecar that handles TLS termination (envoy).

carlos_sre: tagging in — envoy sidecar + keep-alive could be reusing a long-lived upstream connection that still has auth state cached somewhere. Unusual for Redwood (we do per-request auth) but some proxy setups (esp. older enterprise proxies) can do connection-level auth.

alice_support: @carlos_sre do you see anything on the Redwood edge? 

edge-proxy-bot: trace-started: trace_id=tr_0009cd user=bob_merchant path=/v1/chat/completions

carlos_sre: I'm pulling traces now. I see a cluster where requests from the failing host are coming from the same IP and show a sequence: first request after rotation returns 401, subsequent requests from the same TCP connection show 200 again — looks like the upstream connection was re-used but the first handshake used the old key and session cache?

jaya_engineer: quick note: our auth layer is stateless per HTTP request — we always validate Authorization header on each request. The only way Keep-Alive could cause this is if some intermediary rewrote or cached headers. Do we have any logs where the header value differs between client and our edge?

carlos_sre: I grabbed a headers snapshot: incoming from envoy -> our edge:

```
:method: POST
:authority: api.redwood.ai
:scheme: https
authorization: Api-Key sk_live_oldkey_that_was_rotated
content-type: application/json
```

And later requests on same connection show authorization: Api-Key sk_live_newkey_after_rotation

alice_support: So envoy is holding an open upstream connection and sending the old header on the first request after rotation. That implies the sidecar didn't reload the header value for existing connections. Two mitigations: ask customer to restart envoy/sidecar so all upstream connections are re-established, or set Connection: close to force new connection per request.

bob_merchant: Restarting the envoy sidecar fixed it immediately. All hosts are now 200. Wondering if we should change anything on Redwood side to avoid this for other customers?

alice_support: Great fix. For now we'll document guidance. @kevin_custsuccess can we add a note to the KB about rotating keys when using long-lived proxies/sidecars and include steps?

kevin_custsuccess: Yep — will draft KB entry: "If you use sidecars or proxies with long-lived upstream connections, restart or gracefully reconnect them after key rotation; alternatively use Connection: close or short keep-alive timeouts."

jaya_engineer: On product side, we can add a note to the key rotation UI that says "If you use middleware that keeps persistent upstream connections, restart those components after rotation." Low effort. I'll open a ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy-started: kb/support/key-rotation-proxy-note -> staging

alice_support: Action items: 1) kevin to add KB, 2) jaya to open UI-note ticket, 3) carlos to file a short runbook for SRE on detecting mismatch between client header and later requests. I'll mark this resolved for bob_merchant — please re-open if you see 401s again. :thumbsup:

bob_merchant: Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround :raised_hands:
